uncited: **Primitive Generation**: Each occupied voxel is represented by one or more geometric primitives.
**Coordinate Transformation**: Voxel indices $(i, j, k)$ are transformed into world space.
For unit voxels, this simplifies to $P_{world} = I_{voxel} \times V_{size}$, where $V_{size}$ is the voxel dimension .
**Rasterization**: The generated primitives are transformed into clip space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix and rasterized.
**Culling**: To manage performance, frustum culling is applied to exclude voxels outside the camera view.
The approach leverages the parallel processing capabilities of modern GPUs to handle the high vertex counts typical of voxel-based environments.
Early implementations relied on CPU-side mesh generation, which became a bottleneck as world sizes increased.
This technique is widely used in real-time voxel engines, Minecraft-like games, and scientific visualization tools where dynamic terrain modification is required.
